intervals.label: ADONE two-beam data taking for FENICE
intervals.note: Year precision for the start. The same page says elsewhere that 'in 1991, electron-positron operation was resumed to study neutron-antineutron production ... (FENICE experiment)'; 1990 is taken from the sentence that dates the two-beam resumption and the FENICE data taking. The end is the ADONE shutdown on 26 April 1993.
intervals.quote: In 1990, after several years dedicated to single beam operation for synchrotron radiation and nuclear physics, two beam operation with electrons and positrons was resumed to perform the last subnuclear physics experiment, FENICE, whose data taking lasted until the final shutdown of ADONE in 1993.

intervals.label: data taking ended
intervals.note: FENICE data taking 'lasted until the final shutdown of ADONE in 1993'.
intervals.quote: ADONE was shut down on April 26, 1993 to allow the construction of a new low energy, high luminosity collider, DAFNE, inside its building

summary.plain: The FENICE detector at ADONE, built to detect neutron-antineutron pairs from electron-positron annihilation near threshold. The sources fetched do not describe its components.
